# Coverage of the review {#sec-review-map}

The scientific backbone is Sieberer, Buchhold, and Diehl, *Reports on Progress in Physics* **79**, 096001 (2016), DOI [10.1088/0034-4885/79/9/096001](https://doi.org/10.1088/0034-4885/79/9/096001), with the accessible author manuscript [arXiv:1512.00637v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00637v2) [@Sieberer2016]. This map uses the lettered subsection notation of its PDF. The experimental HTML conversion sometimes numbers these subsections instead.

Coverage means that the book develops the section's physical question, model, method, and central results in an independent exposition. It does not reproduce every historical citation, sentence, equation number, or published graphic. Review equations are rederived with the conventions in @sec-conventions. When a numerical result comes from a cited paper, it is identified as such rather than presented as a calculation performed for this book.

The review's acknowledgements (VII) are the original authors' personal statements and are not teaching content to reproduce. Its bibliography is represented here by citations to the review and to the primary papers used in developing each topic. @sec-laboratory and @sec-conventions are additional teaching material.

## Reading routes

For a first course, read prerequisites → contour → Gaussian theory → classical fields → symmetries, and then choose an application. For a critical-phenomena course, add renormalization → condensation → KPZ. For nonequilibrium dynamics, add heating and reproduce the numerical laboratory. The spin-glass chapter uses bilocal kernels and benefits from studying Gaussian elimination and the effective-action construction first.

A useful assessment is to derive the lossy cavity's occupation without a path integral, derive it again from $G^K$, and explain why the result is not generally a thermal fluctuation-dissipation relation. This connects the microscopic and field-theoretic descriptions before moving to an interacting application.
